Subject: Inference economics initiation + implementation roadmap

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. To keep momentum on the pilot, here’s a compact starting plan focused on cost/perf tuning during onboarding (batching, caching, quantization profile selection, routing). Goal is to get a stable canary in production within 6 weeks. Proposed high-level steps: 

• Kickoff & data intake (this week): profile traffic shape (seq length distribution, concurrency), SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets), and cost targets.
• Baseline run (week 1): enable default batching + no quantization, collect token counts and latency histograms.
• Quantization profiling (week 2–3): test 8-bit/4-bit variants on representative prompts, measure quality regressions using your prompt set.
• Caching & prefix/KV policy (week 2–4): identify hot prefixes, enable KV cache, assess hit rate changes.
• Routing & fallback policy (week 3–5): configure fast/cheap variant routing with graceful fallbacks for tail latency.
• Canary & tune (week 5–6): rollout canary, monitor token costs, latency SLOs, and user-facing quality metrics; adjust batching windows and cache TTLs.

Action items for GreenMetrics before kickoff:
1) Share a small sample of representative prompts (50–100) and a day’s request logs or a small aggregation of sequence length distribution.
2) Confirm latency and cost targets (p95 target, cost per 1k tokens budget).
3) Provide the procurement contact so we can circulate the SOW.

I’ve attached a draft SOW and a starter CSV for quantization profiles we’ll use to capture quality metrics. Suggest a 45-minute kickoff — are you available Wed 7/16 at 10am PT or Fri 7/18 at 9am PT?

Best,
Naomi
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Tom/Naomi — quick technical notes ahead of kickoff: 

1) Quantization: For a first pass we’ll evaluate two profiles — 8-bit asymmetric (fast, safe) and 4-bit (aggressive, higher compute-density). I attached a starter CSV to capture model/temperature/prompt-category/quality-metric columns so we can track regressions per profile.
2) Batching: we need realistic concurrency estimates. If you typically see short bursts (10–20 reqs/sec) we’ll target a batching window of 15–25ms and a max batch size of 64. If bursts are larger, we’ll propose dynamic batching with size caps.
3) KV caching: we’ll instrument prefix hashes; please confirm whether prompts include any session identifiers we should strip before caching.

Attachments: quant_profiles.csv (starter).

I’ll bring a short runner script to the kickoff that can ingest your sample prompts and produce latency/cost baselines in <1 hour.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
